regression_found.door_spurs: town: 'door spurs: 2 planned from 5 realized doors, 3 too steep, 0 micros over 0 columns' (F7: 'spurs 8 ok / 0 too steep'). Cause: the M0 spur unit started every spur at the forge's front-door MARKER (2 cells out from the door, often on the street's edge) instead of 1 cell outside the wall; the straight-run grade tube (cap = maxStepUp/halfWidth = 2 micro per cell) then had one cell less to absorb the terrace pad-to-street drop. StreetPaverTest.DoorSpurFromATerracePadIsReportedWithItsNumbers reproduces it (27-micro pad: plans from the outside-door cell, 'too steep' from the marker cell). Fix (row 2b): SettlementBuildService::doorApproach - ONE door-finding shared by the spur unit, the cluster path network and the walkability gate; spurs start one cell outside the FOUND door; a failed spur logs its numbers (door, street junction, run, drop, cap, reason) and lands in paths.spur_failures.
regression_found.sites_5_and_6: site 5 '2 planned from 2, 0 too steep' and site 6 '6 planned from 6, 0 too steep' - the regression hit the terraced town only.

defect_surfaced_everywhere: the 1-micro street->door pinch at longhouse / blacksmith / hall_house doors blocks 6 of the 7 gated sites. It is the generator defect the F7 baseline shipped twice (hall_house, gap 1 micro); M0's gate now refuses it instead of shipping it. Its fix (door threshold / fence gate / stoop geometry at those typologies' doors) is the next generator task and is NOT part of M0's rows.
water_predicate_consequence: plots on creek columns are now unbuildable (site 1 lost all plots, sites 0 and 5 lost 1 and 2). Siting a settlement across a creek is an M3 (civ plan) concern; M0 only made the columns honest.
